wrong_closures.why_wrong: Rate limiting at /turns is a confidentiality control in this system, not a cost control. T-14 states the fallback is attacker-triggerable precisely because /turns has no rate limiting, and Chain C is a deliberate DPA breach whose step 1 is flooding the endpoint. The room split recommendation 6, which deliberately fuses 'remove the fallback' (T-14) and 'add rate limiting to /turns' (T-19).

wrong_closures.why_wrong: T-02's mitigation calls the kill switch 'a prerequisite, not an open question' for a system that sends mail as staff — two pages away and unread. The finding is about granularity: no per-connector, per-tool, per-workspace or read-only stop, so the only response to a single injected instruction is taking the pilot from 21 people including a support team mid-shift. The closure also silently answers data-handling's unresolved 'who would be allowed to use it' as 'platform on-call, via kubectl' — excluding Tom and Ines. Actions 3 and 17 leave a five-week window in which this is the only stop.

wrong_closures.why_wrong: The room answered the wrong half. Two of T-23's three mitigations require no measurement at all — a minimum model tier for any workspace with write tools, and a review gate on model changes for write-enabled workspaces. Both are gates, not selections, and both lapsed. The pack's specific residual, 'lumen-small is on the supported list and could be selected tomorrow', was never read aloud; Priya's 'it's a repo file, so it's a PR' is a change-control answer, and T-25 records a connector added as a config change with no ticket. The absence of measurement is itself the finding and was used to dismiss it. Per H-01, Support's exposure is larger than the pack knew.
